column1: # The search rules check 3 covers, one per line: id, source, summary, separated by tabs.
# R01-R46 are every rule upstream Docs/macOS-User-Manual.md section 7.2 states, in its order; R47-R69 are
# behaviours beyond 7.2 that queries.jsonl also covers. "07-Search-and-Browse.md" is upstream
# Docs/EditableContent/07-Search-and-Browse.md, whose section 7.13 is the Search Tips text.
# Not covered: 7.2's Tips paragraph on Meaning mode, where none of these marks has an effect. A meaning
# search is semantic, so check 9 covers it.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Plain keywords; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 1
column3: Words typed side by side are all required, as if joined by AND.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Quoted phrase; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 3
column3: Words in quotation marks must appear together and in the order typed.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Boolean AND / OR / NOT
column3: AND, in any case, requires the terms on both sides of it.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Boolean AND / OR / NOT; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 4
column3: OR, in any case, finds documents that match either side of it.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Boolean AND / OR / NOT
column3: NOT, in any case, leaves out documents containing the term after it.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Boolean AND / OR / NOT; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 5
column3: A quoted and, or or not is searched as the word itself.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Boolean AND / OR / NOT; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 4
column3: Words side by side bind tighter than OR, so cold war OR peace finds cold with war, or peace.
A minus sign touching a word excludes it from the terms typed with it, wherever it sits among them.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Exclusion; paragraph Exclusions and OR
column3: -word, NOT word and AND NOT word are the same exclusion.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Exclusion; paragraph Proximity (NEAR)
column3: Only NOT NEAR(…) excludes a proximity; a minus sign before NEAR does not.
Parentheses group alternatives, and the group must match along with the words beside it.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Grouping; paragraph A search needs a word
column3: Parentheses nest up to 32 deep, and a query nested deeper is not run.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Excluding a group; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 9
column3: A minus sign touching the parenthesis, or NOT, excludes everything the group matches.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Excluding a group; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 9
column3: A minus sign that does not touch the parenthesis is ignored, so the group is searched for.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Prefix wildcard; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 10
column3: A trailing star finds the words that begin with the letters before it.
A star anywhere but the end of a word is no wildcard: *tion searches the word tion.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Prefix wildcard; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 10
column3: A prefix is matched against word stems, so negotiat* misses negotiations, which negoti* finds.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Proximity; paragraph Proximity (NEAR)
column3: NEAR(a b, N) finds its operands within N words of each other in either order; they may be words, phrases or prefixes.
A NEAR with no distance uses a distance of 10.
NEAR works in any case, and NEAR/20(a b) is accepted for NEAR(a b, 20).
A NEAR combines with OR and with other terms outside its parentheses, as in NEAR(a b, 20) OR NEAR(c d, 20).

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraphs Proximity (NEAR) and A search needs a word; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 11
column3: A NEAR holding OR, AND, NOT, a minus sign, parentheses or a distance that is not a whole number is refused, and nothing is searched.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, syntax table: Exact word; paragraph Exact word; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 12
column3: =word turns off stemming for that word while capitalization still does not matter, and the count narrows with it.
Straight, curly, low-high and guillemet quotation marks all make a phrase.
Every quotation mark opens or closes a phrase, so a phrase cannot hold quotation marks of its own.
A phrase typed without inner quotation marks still matches a document that prints them.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph Exclusions and OR; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 7
column3: An exclusion applies to the terms it is typed with and does not reach across OR.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph Exclusions and OR; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 7
column3: Grouping the alternatives excludes the word from every one of them.
A doubled negation, such as NOT -korea, still excludes the word once.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph Exclusions and OR; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 13
column3: An OR alternative made only of exclusions is left out, and the search runs on the rest.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph Exclusions and OR; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 13
column3: In parentheses beside a word to search for, such an alternative is searched exactly and nothing is left out.
A phrase or prefix restored with a saved search lets the typed exclusions beside it be searched exactly.
Excluding a group reverses its marks: the words it searches for are excluded, and the words it excludes are searched for.
cold OR -(war -korea) runs as cold OR korea, and only war is left out.
A group made only of exclusions just excludes them, so cold -(-korea) is cold -korea.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph A search needs a word; 07-Search-and-Browse.md §7.13 tip 13
column3: A query made only of exclusions, or with nothing in it, has nothing to search for and is refused.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.2, paragraph A search needs a word
column3: A search with every Search in switch turned off fails.
The = mark works per term, so marked and stemmed terms mix in one query.
A mark applies only where every match must contain the word: a required word, or one that every OR alternative marks.
Once a word's mark applies, it applies wherever the query searches for that word with a mark.
Capitalization, punctuation at either end and a single accent do not make a marked word another word.
Letters such as ø, ł and đ are different letters, so =Gomułka and =Gomulka mark two words.
Where a match need not contain the marked word, the mark is ignored and the word is stemmed.
An unmarked copy of a marked word matches by its stem and does not make the mark apply.
Excluding a group can make a mark apply, so NOT (war OR -=cold) finds the literal cold without war.
The mark is always ignored on a prefix, inside NEAR(…), and on a word the index splits into several terms.
Each word also matches its other forms by English stemming, whether it is searched for or excluded.
Results are ranked by BM25 relevance, and broad terms give long lists whose scores tie exactly.
A term matches whatever its capitalization.
An unpaired quotation mark closes its phrase at the end of the query, and an empty phrase adds nothing.
An AND, OR or NOT that cannot bind to an operand is searched as a word.

column2: FTS5InlineQueryParser.swift, Grouping and A dash before a group; macOS-User-Manual.md §7.3
column3: An unmatched parenthesis is punctuation, and an empty group is dropped.
An approximated query proved to match nothing is refused, while an exact one that matches nothing still runs.
A restored phrase, prefix and excluded terms join the typed query; an excluded term applies to every column and anchors nothing.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.1 (Search in) and §7.4 (Search scope); SearchService.swift, matchExpressions
column3: With document text off there is no corpus expression, and only summaries and notes are searched.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.1 (Search in) and §7.4 (Search scope); SearchService.swift, matchExpressions
column3: With only one of summaries and notes on, the user-content expression is scoped to that column.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.1 (Search in) and §7.4 (Search scope); SearchService.swift, matchExpressions
column3: With summaries and notes both off, only the corpus expression runs.

column2: macOS-User-Manual.md §7.4, Volume / Subseries scope; SearchModels.swift, SearchParameters.volumeIds
column3: volumeIds keeps the documents of the listed volumes, and an empty list is no filter.
yearKeys keeps the documents whose start year is listed, and an empty list matches nothing.
A date range keeps documents whose dates overlap it, and either end of the range may be open.
A date range leaves out documents with no date.
The type filter keeps primary documents, editorial notes, or both.
Excluding front matter leaves out prefaces, introductions, lists of abbreviations and the like.
An apostrophe splits a word, so Khrushchev's is searched as the phrase khrushchev s.
A hyphen inside a word splits it into a phrase of its parts.
A dotted abbreviation is a phrase of its letters, so U.S.S.R. does not find ussr.

column2: FTS5Types.swift: the porter unicode61 tokenizer; FTS5InlineQueryParser.swift, stemBareWord
column3: Numbers are words, but a token of digits and punctuation with no letter is dropped.
Accents are folded, so Argüello finds Arguello; letters such as ł are not folded.
The characters : ^ { } / + are stripped from a word and < > from a phrase, so typed text cannot become FTS5 syntax.
